TSMC holds 301 US patents granted since 2001, with recent grants covering semiconductor fabrication, device manufacturing, ESD protection, and power management, but the dataset records no AI-specific products or lawsuits.

The recent patents span process technology, device structure, and circuit-level reliability, indicating ongoing work across the full semiconductor manufacturing stack. The company profile describes TSMC as the world's dedicated semiconductor foundry since 1987, supporting an ecosystem of customers with process technology and design enablement. That position matters for AI because advanced chips are the compute substrate, but this data does not link any specific patent to AI workloads.

The dataset records no AI-specific products, lawsuits, or MCP servers for TSMC, so it cannot support claims about the company's direct AI strategy or legal exposure. The patent count comes from USPTO grants since 2001 using the applicant phrase "tsmc", which may undercount international filings or subsidiaries. It also does not include fab locations, energy use, or grid constraints, so it says nothing about the power or building side of AI scaling.
